title: Centripetal Acceleration: Steering, Not Speeding
topic: Centripetal acceleration — uniform circular motion gives a = v²/r = rω², always pointing toward the centre

beats.narration: Whirl a ball around at constant speed — same speed, curved path, and it is still accelerating. How?

elements.content: Manimo bobs in centre-screen
Constant speed, curved path — yet it's accelerating.

beats.narration: A ball moving in a circle keeps turning. Even at constant speed, the velocity vector keeps changing direction — and a change in velocity is acceleration.

elements.content: Dashed circle of radius 130 centred at (440, 200)
Centre dot at the circle's centre
Orbiting ball (amber, radius 14) revolving once every 4 seconds
Velocity vector tangent to the circle, anchored at the ball, rotates with it
v label near the velocity arrowhead
same speed, but the velocity vector keeps turning

beats.narration: That acceleration always points inward, toward the centre of the circle. Its size is the speed squared divided by the radius.

elements.content: Same dashed circle (smaller, radius 100) at (440, 130)
Orbiting ball revolving once every 4 seconds
Velocity vector tangent to circle (rose)
Centripetal acceleration vector pointing from ball toward centre
a_c label near the inward arrow
a_c = v²/r
elements.position: below the diagram, large amber payoff

elements.content: always inward — toward the centre of the curve

beats.narration: Substitute v equals r omega, and the same acceleration becomes r omega squared.

elements.content: v = rω
a_c = v²/r
a_c = rω²
two ways of saying the same thing

beats.narration: Centripetal acceleration sits perpendicular to the motion at every instant — so it does no work. It does not speed the ball up. It just steers.

elements.content: Always perpendicular to v — does no work.
It doesn't speed the ball up — it just steers.
(no work, no energy spent — pure direction change)
